## isva-p06-v46 — C1

**SUMMARY.** From change, that One is longed for by all spirits — yet body's change runs by nature. As before, why not for the deemed-freed? It occurs, yet joins him not. Done and need-free he stands alone — yet needlessness fits no spirit ever, nor mind. With need gone, no meeting again — yet minds are born in bodies still. If sense-bound nature, not karma's waning, mokṣa is mere nature on karma's prop. Knowers act from compassion — yet passionless, release is passion's waning. Drop the nature-view, unjust; bodies bespeak a knowing Maker. From patterned difference, flawless proof — laid on the Lord by self-entrusted hand, unshaken.

*Rasa: vīra (triumph) of the sealed proof — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: freed-spirit tests failing, mokṣa-into-nature absurd, compassion betraying passion — then abandonment, proof, aim. Triumph relished.*
